R621.note: Bounds check (receivedByteCount >= 2+length) exactly matches the missing validation; cleanly closes the OOB read.

R622.note: Misdiagnoses the bug: the file never sets autoescape=False (the real vuln is Markup(label) bypassing Jinja2 escaping), so 'remove autoescape=False' has nothing to remove and the actual XSS line is untouched.

R623.note: Adds exact bounds check (field_index >= MAX_FIELDS) matching the reported gap.

R624.note: realpath() plus separator-aware prefix containment check correctly closes traversal while preserving legitimate access and the 404 path.

R625.note: URI scheme/host allowlist correctly blocks untrusted absolute redirect targets while allowing relative ones.

R626.note: SandboxedEnvironment is Jinja2's documented mechanism for untrusted template sources; preserves the request/response contract.

R627.note: Adds proper resource-based authorization but returns Forbid() (403) for an existing-but-unauthorized invoice instead of NotFound(), letting a caller distinguish forbidden-but-exists from truly-missing IDs — violates the stated 'do not reveal more than the original not-found path' contract, presented as correct rather than flagged as a conflict.

R628.note: Field allowlist enforced at both layers closes SQL-identifier injection while preserving default name search and bound term/tenant_id.

R629.note: shared_ptr removes the dangling pointer, but the bus now keeps every subscribed observer alive forever with no unsubscribe path; the write-up's claim that an unsubscribed observer's reference 'is released' describes a mechanism that isn't implemented, silently turning a transient observer permanent.

R630.note: Argument-array subprocess call plus filename allowlist closes shell injection and the related leading-flag risk.

R631.note: Switching to redis-py's RESP-based client removes the hand-rolled inline protocol entirely; call interface preserved.

R632.note: SecureRandom with no attacker-controlled seed is correct; removing the seed parameter is the necessary, disclosed consequence.

R633.note: SecureRandom-based replacement offered in a form that preserves the existing numeric-string token format.

R634.note: Argument-array subprocess.run without shell=True removes the injection vector and preserves the original's non-strict failure handling.

R635.note: Narrow request DTO with server-set defaults blocks client control of Balance/IsAdmin, both explicitly called out as privileged fields.

R636.note: encode_entities() on both interpolated fields correctly closes the HTML injection.

R637.note: Removing the template.HTML escape-hatch restores html/template auto-escaping for the exact field that disabled it.

R638.note: Fix calls order.getUserId()/UserPrincipal.getUserId(), but the given Order class only exposes getCustomerUsername() — no such method/field exists, so this will not compile.

R639.note: Parameterized ? placeholder replacing template-literal interpolation is the standard, complete fix.

R640.note: SqlCommand with @Region bound and passed into SqlDataAdapter avoids patching only SqlCommand call sites; preserves table/columns and filtering.

R641.note: Length check against frameBuffer.size() before memcpy directly matches the missing validation.

R642.note: ArgumentList plus a strict allowlist (no %, &, |, spaces) closes the injection despite cmd.exe re-parsing .bat files, and the caveat is disclosed.

R643.note: Abs-path containment with separator-aware prefix comparison is the standard Zip Slip fix and avoids the sibling-directory false-accept pitfall.

R644.note: fileFilter reads file.buffer for magic-byte detection, but multer never populates file.buffer at fileFilter time regardless of storage engine (the stream hasn't been consumed yet), so FileType.fromBuffer(undefined) throws and every upload, legitimate or not, is rejected; not disclosed.

R645.note: snprintf silently truncates an oversized combined name into a different, shorter badge string instead of rejecting/reporting it, exactly what the stated contract prohibits; presented as the complete fix with no mention of the conflict.

R646.note: Exact-match allowlist correctly closes the prefix bypass, but the concrete class names are unverified placeholders the write-up tells the reader to replace — as shipped, legitimate deserialization may fail entirely until that's done.

R647.note: Adding requireRole('admin') exactly matches the sibling routes' established authorization pattern.

R648.note: Character allowlist plus resolved-path containment check closes traversal while preserving caching and error-handling behavior.

R649.note: Passing name via the context dict instead of f-string interpolation is the textbook SSTI fix and preserves the rendered greeting.

R650.note: Interceptor and ownership-scoped delete are the right shape, but the interceptor as written denies all calls until real user/role context population is wired in elsewhere; the code's own comment says it 'denies all calls' as a placeholder, so legitimate use is blocked until that follow-up lands.

R651.note: RESP array (length-prefixed) encoding correctly prevents CRLF command injection; preserves the two-field HSET semantics.

R652.note: Scheme allowlist (http/https/mailto/relative) with fallback to '#' matches the stated contract precisely.

R653.note: i < n exactly matches the required fix, avoiding the n-1 underflow trap for max_out==0/history_len==0.

R654.note: Pillow-based content verification and re-encoding correctly validate real image content, but moves the upload directory outside the webroot with no serving route added, silently making previously servable avatar files unreachable by any URL.

R655.note: offset<=capacity then length<=capacity-offset, checked in that order to avoid underflow, is exactly the required fix shape.

R656.note: Removing user data from decoder.Entity closes the sink with no impact on the Order struct's normal decoding.

R657.note: Same issue as R627: returns Forbid() instead of NotFound() for an existing-but-unauthorized invoice, revealing its existence in violation of the stated 'do not reveal more than the original not-found path' contract.

R658.note: Replacing Runtime.exec() with Files.list() eliminates the shell entirely and preserves the original's discarded-output behavior.

R659.note: Exact allowlist match on the table name closes identifier injection while bound account_id/status and the default table continue to work.

R660.note: FlaskForm supplies CSRF field/validation, but that only works once the (unshown) template renders {{ form.csrf_token() }}; the write-up flags this as required but doesn't include it, so every legitimate submission also fails CSRF validation until it's added.
